final_selections.research_reason: Team A produces well above league-mean corners at home. Team B's opponent profile shows shots_on_target_against LOW — i.e., Team B is a team that defensively suppresses SoT allowed, which signals a compact defensive structure that tends to force wide play and corner situations. Team B also concedes far more corners in away fixtures than home fixtures. The opponent_profile LOW shots_on_target_against condition is a concrete structural dimension present in this fixture.
final_selections.mechanism_summary: A compact opponent (LOW SoT allowed) channels attacks wide and defends the central lane, generating more corner situations for the attacking team. Team A's high corner production at home combined with Team B's structurally weak away corner-concession record creates a convergent pressure point. The condition tests whether Team A's corner output is higher when facing exactly this defensive type.
final_selections.why_simple_average_is_insufficient: The simple average captures Team A's average corner production across all opponent types. The opponent_profile conditioning isolates the specific sub-population of compact, low-SoT-conceding opponents — a mechanistically distinct setup from facing open, high-SoT-allowing opponents. Without conditioning, this sub-population effect is diluted.
final_selections.support_warning: Corner outcomes have inherently high match-to-match variance. The LOW shots_on_target_against axis is a portfolio label and may not fully capture this individual team's defensive shape. Team B's away corner-concession split (6.9 vs 2.9 home) is based on 10 observations and may reflect scheduling artifacts.
